UNESCO grades languages mainly by how far down the generations they are still used at home. Revival happens: Hebrew went from written and liturgical use back to everyday street speech 🌍.

prompt: is it true that most indian scripts are cousins of each other
reply:
Yes, and the family resemblance is structural, not just visual. Tamil, Devanagari, Telugu, Bengali and several South-East Asian scripts all descend from Brahmi, in use in India over two thousand years ago. That shared ancestor is why they share deep habits: a consonant carries a built-in vowel, and vowel marks hang above, below or beside it. Latin letters come from a different line, through Phoenician and Greek 🌳.
